sections.label: Singapore ivory seizure 2019
sections.summary: Singapore seized a record haul of elephant ivory worth over S$170 million from more than 300 African elephants in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For example, through our close collaboration with our counterparts in China, we seized a record haul of elephant ivory passing through Singapore in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The ivory was worth more than S$170 million and it came from more than 300 African elephants.

sections.label: Ivory ban and ESA amendments
sections.summary: A domestic ivory trade ban has been in place since last September, and ESA amendments are proposed to strengthen CITES trade regulations, penalties and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For example, through ESA, we have established a domestic ban in ivory trade since last September, to support international efforts against the illegal trade in elephant ivory.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: We are now proposing to amend ESA, to strengthen our regulations for the trade of CITES species, and to enhance our penalties and enforcement powers against such illegal trade.

sections.label: Four aims of ESA amendments
sections.summary: The amendments aim to strengthen CITES trade regulation, align ESA with CITES Resolutions, stiffen penalties, and strengthen NParks' enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: First, to strengthen Singapore's regulatory regime for trade in CITES species; second, to align ESA more closely with CITES Resolutions; third, to introduce stiffer penalties for illegal trade for CITES species; and fourth, to strengthen NParks' enforcement powers so that it can tackle illegal wildlife trade more effectively.

sections.label: Transit traders destination document
sections.summary: Clause 3 requires traders bringing CITES species in transit to give NParks a document naming a destination outside Singapore, issued within set dates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 3 therefore replaces this requirement with a stipulation that traders who bring CITES species in transit through Singapore must among other things, provide NParks with a document that specifies a port, airport or any other place outside Singapore as the destination for the CITES species.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This document must also be issued on or before, or within 14 days after the date on which the CITES species is brought into Singapore.

sections.label: Hybrid animals under ESA
sections.summary: Clause 2 amends ESA so regulations apply to hybrid animals of CITES species as though they are full species.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 2 amends ESA to make clear that our regulations apply to hybrid animals of CITES species, as though they are full species.

sections.label: Retrospective and altered documents rejected
sections.summary: Clauses 4 and 5 make clear that retrospectively issued or unauthorisedly altered permits and certificates are not accepted for CITES species trade in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Lastly, clauses 4 and 5 make clear that permits, certificates or any other similar documents issued retrospectively after the date of the export or re-export of the CITES species, or that contain unauthorised alterations, are not accepted for the trade of CITES species in Singapore.

sections.label: Higher penalties for illegal wildlife trade
sections.summary: Clause 4 raises the maximum fine for illegal trade in Appendix I species from $50,000 to $100,000 and imprisonment from two to six years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 4 increases the maximum fine for illegal trade in Appendix I species, from $50,000 to $100,000, and the maximum imprisonment term, from two years to six years.

sections.label: Fines for corporate CITES offenders
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends ESA to raise maximum fines for corporate offenders trading CITES species to $200,000 per Appendix I specimen and $100,000 per Appendix II or III specimen.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 4 will also amend ESA to increase the maximum fine for corporate offenders who illegally trade in CITES species, up to $200,000 for each specimen of an Appendix I species and up to $100,000 for each specimen of an Appendix II or III species.

sections.label: Maximum aggregate fines for offenders
sections.summary: Maximum aggregate fines are set at $500,000 for individuals and $1,000,000 for corporate offenders, or the species' market value, whichever is higher.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The maximum aggregate fines for individual offenders will be set at $500,000 or $1,000,000 for individual and corporate offenders respectively, or the market value of the CITES species at the material time of the offence, whichever is higher.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As rhinoceros horns are worth over $30,000 per kilogramme, the offender could face a maximum aggregate fine of $760,000, if he had been subject to the stiffer penalties in the Bill, instead of the $500,000 today.

sections.label: Conveyances exempt from forfeiture
sections.summary: Under clause 9, large conveyances over 200 tonnes net, aircraft and trains on regular passenger service, and conveyances used without the owner's consent may not be forfeited.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Under clause 9, large conveyances of more than 200 tonnes net and aircraft and trains used for regular passenger service to and from Singapore, as well as conveyances that were used unlawfully without the owner's consent, may not be forfeited.

sections.label: Court ordered forfeiture replaces mandatory
sections.summary: Clause 9 replaces mandatory forfeiture with Court ordered forfeiture in criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 9 replaces such mandatory forfeiture with Court ordered forfeiture in criminal proceedings.

sections.label: NParks seized animals sold online
sections.summary: In 2021, NParks seized more than 90 animals sold online as exotic pets, and thirteen individuals are under investigation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: In 2021, NParks seized more than 90 animals that were being sold online as exotic pets, in an island-wide raid.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Thirteen individuals are currently under investigation for the sale of these animals.

sections.label: Pangolin and ivory seizures
sections.summary: Singapore seized 12.9 tonnes of pangolin scales from Nigeria and 8.8 tonnes of ivory in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In April 2019, we broke the record by finding 12.9 tonnes of pangolin scales being smuggled in a shipment from Nigeria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This was worth over $50 million and cost the lives of over 17,000 pangolins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three months after that, we seized a shipment of 8.8 tonnes of ivory, estimated to come from nearly 300 African elephants.

sections.label: Wildlife trafficking under Organised Crime Act
sections.summary: The speaker proposes categorising wildlife trafficking as serious offences under the Organised Crime Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first proposal is that we categorise wildlife trafficking as serious offences under the Organised Crime Act (or OCA).

sections.label: OCA purpose and prevention
sections.summary: The speaker says OCA aims to prevent organised crime taking root, so laws should be strengthened before syndicates are rooted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us remember that OCA was enacted not only to combat existing threats of organised crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As described by Minister Iswaran when passing OCA, it is meant to "prevent organised crime from taking root in Singapore." Let us not wait until we prosecute a confirmed syndicate member and when illegal wildlife trade syndicates are deeply rooted in Singapore before we strengthen our laws.

sections.label: Hong Kong wildlife crime amendment
sections.summary: Hong Kong recently amended its Organised and Serious Crimes Ordinance to include wildlife crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recently, Hong Kong also amended its "Organised and Serious Crimes Ordinance" to include wildlife crime as an organised and serious crime.

sections.label: Fines three times market value
sections.summary: The speaker proposes increasing fines to three times the market value of the specimens involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Instead, I propose that the fines be increased to three times the market value of the specimens involved.

sections.label: Treat wildlife trade as organised crime
sections.summary: The speaker says it is time to treat the illegal wildlife trade as the serious organised crime it is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I, for one, am not willing to look my children in the eye and say that we were the generation that let this happen on our watch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is time to treat the illegal wildlife trade as the serious organised crime that it is.

sections.label: Organised crime and wildlife
sections.summary: Organised criminal networks add to their profits by being involved in wildlife crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Organised criminal networks are adding to their profits through involvement in wildlife crime.

sections.label: Wildlife crime and border smuggling
sections.summary: Tackling illegal wildlife crime could make it easier to halt gun and drug shipments and to arrest trafficking kingpins or middlemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To acknowledge that the steps you take to tackle illegal wildlife crime could make it easier to halt the shipments of guns and drugs passing through your borders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: You might find it easier to arrest a kingpin or a middleman for trafficking illegal wildlife products than to catch him red-handed smuggling heroin.

sections.label: Bengal cat trade under Bill
sections.summary: The Bill as it stands would let a fifth-generation Bengal cat be freely traded in Singapore without documentation on the original leopard cat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill, as it stands, would allow a fifth-generation Bengal cat to be freely traded in Singapore, without requiring any documentation on when, where or how the original leopard cat was purveyed.

sections.label: Singapore jail term for wildlife trafficking
sections.summary: Singapore's maximum jail term for wildlife trafficking is said to be ASEAN's lowest, and a seven-year term can be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore’s maximum jail term for wildlife trafficking is still, to my understanding, the lowest penalty in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to position Singapore as a regional leader in the fight against illegal wildlife trade, a harsher jail term of seven years can be considered.

sections.label: Internet advertising endangered wildlife
sections.summary: The Internet is used as a tool for these trades, and advertising endangered wildlife online should be an offence if the transactions would be illegal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These examples demonstrate the extent to which the Internet is used as a tool in conducting such deplorable trades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose that advertising endangered wildlife or wildlife products on these online platforms should also be treated as an offence if those transactions would be illegal under the law.

sections.label: Protected animal and plant species
sections.summary: Almost 6,000 animal and 33,000 plant species are currently protected against over-exploitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At present, almost 6,000 animal and 33,000 plant species are protected against over-exploitation.

sections.label: Asian elephant and pangolin decline
sections.summary: Asian elephant numbers fell 50% in a century and Asian pangolins are heavily poached, so Singapore can go beyond CITES.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Southeast Asia, the Asian Elephant population has declined by 50% over the past century.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The four species of Asian pangolins are now among most poached animals in the world, by some reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But going forward, Singapore can go further and can do more to demonstrate forward thinking and leadership on this issue by going beyond CITES.

sections.label: Proposed higher wildlife trade penalties
sections.summary: The speaker proposes raising ESA prison sentences to at least five years and fines to three times market value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Following the amendments, persons prosecuted under the Endangered Species Act (ESA) would receive a maximum of four years' prison sentence and a fine of up to $500,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is paltry, compared to $66 million, the value of a single shipment of elephant ivory and pangolin scales intercepted in Singapore in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I propose that the prison sentence should be raised to no less than five years for deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The aggregate fine should be three times the market value of the goods, aligning it with the Customs Act.

sections.label: Vets reporting illegal exotic pets
sections.summary: The passage asks whether vets must report exotic pets that are illegal or suspected to be illegally procured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are vets required to make a report if they come across an exotic pet that is illegal or suspected to be procured through illegal means?

sections.label: Illegal wildlife trade ranking
sections.summary: Illegal wildlife trade is the fourth largest trade, Singapore contributes to CITES and INTERPOL, and exotic pets are non-essential luxuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The illegal wildlife trade is the fourth largest trade behind drugs, human trafficking and counterfeiting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am glad to know that we actively contributing to CITES and the INTERPOL Wildlife Crime Working Group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Ultimately, exotic pets and their by-products are non-essential luxuries.

sections.label: Enhanced CITES penalty framework
sections.summary: Fines and jail terms for illegal CITES species trade are increased, with maximum aggregate fines matching market value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: That is why we have further enhanced our penalty framework, following feedback from the public consultation exercise we went through earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will increase the fines and jail terms that can be meted out for individuals who illegally trade in CITES species as well as penalties for the domestic trade in CITES species to align with that for international trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In addition, the maximum aggregate fine will be raised across the board to match the market value of all illegally traded CITES species comprised in the offence, where the market value is higher than the maximum aggregate fine of $500,000 or $1,000,000 for individual and corporate offenders respectively.

sections.label: Seizure of concealment items
sections.summary: The Bill introduces provisions allowing seizure or forfeiture of items used to conceal CITES species and their conveyances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In addition, the Bill will introduce provisions to allow for the seizure or forfeiture of items used to conceal CITES species as well as their conveyances.

sections.label: Buying illegally traded CITES species
sections.summary: Buyers of illegally traded CITES species can already be penalised, but Members suggested explicitly including buying as an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Although buyers of illegally traded CITES species can already be penalised under the Act, Members such as Mr Louis Ng suggested to explicitly include the act of buying as an offence in the Act.

sections.label: NParks charges over five years
sections.summary: Over five years, NParks charged eight persons for possession and three for facilitating sale of illegally traded CITES species.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Over the last five years, NParks has used these provisions to charge eight persons for the possession of illegally traded CITES species and three persons for facilitating the sale of such species.

sections.label: Island-wide wildlife seizure operations
sections.summary: Last year NParks carried out two island-wide operations and seized over 90 wildlife specimens from online sellers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Just last year, NParks carried out two island-wide operations and seized more than 90 wildlife specimens, including some CITES species, from sellers who had listed them on social media and e-commerce platforms.

sections.label: Boa constrictor case and stiffer penalties
sections.summary: In 2020 NParks charged an individual over a boa constrictor; the Bill proposes fines up to $100,000 and six years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For example, in 2020, NParks charged an individual for the illegal possession and sale of a boa constrictor, which is listed in CITES Appendix II, on the online messaging service, Telegram.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: With the amendments proposed in this Bill, such offenders will be subject to stiffer penalties, including a monetary fine of up to $100,000 and a maximum imprisonment term of up to six years for the sale and advertisement of illegally traded CITES species.

sections.label: Informers and reward programme
sections.summary: NParks receives tip-offs, amendments protect informers' identities, and a reward programme is being explored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Indeed, NParks will receive tip-offs from time to time to enforce against illegal wildlife trafficking and that is why we have made amendments to protect the identity of these informers, which may encourage more persons to provide information about such illegal activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We are in the midst of exploring the feasibility of a reward programme, to further encourage informers to step forward.

sections.label: Permits for Bengal Cat trade
sections.summary: When the amendments come into force, traders must provide permits for the trade of Bengal Cats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Moving forward, when the amendments to the Act come into force, it will be a requirement in the ESA for traders to provide these permits for the trade of such Bengal Cats.

sections.label: Centre for Wildlife Forensics
sections.summary: The Centre for Wildlife Forensics was set up and became a CITES reference laboratory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For example, earlier in my speech, I said that we set up the Centre for Wildlife Forensics, which became a CITES reference laboratory.

sections.label: Illegal wildlife trade as organised crime
sections.summary: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Louis Ng asked for illegal wildlife trade to be recognised as a serious organised crime in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To enhance our levers to combat illegal wildlife trade, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Louis Ng asked for illegal wildlife trade to be recognised as a serious organised crime in Singapore.

sections.label: Partnerships against illegal wildlife trade
sections.summary: NParks and WWF-Singapore held roundtables with online platforms and shipping representatives, and amendments strengthen CITES trade regulations, penalties and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: NParks and the World Wide Fund for Nature-Singapore have jointly organised roundtable discussions with the Coalition to End Wildlife Trafficking Online, which includes digital platforms such as Facebook, or Meta, TikTok, Lazada and Carousell, to raise awareness on the illegal sale of exotic pets online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In January this year, they also jointly engaged over 80 representatives from the shipping industry, to share best practices for tackling the illegal trade in wildlife.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Overall, the amendments will help to strengthen our regulations for the trade of CITES species and to enhance our penalties and enforcement powers against such illegal trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The fight also goes beyond Singapore and requires strong cooperation at the bilateral, regional and international levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will continue to partner with the international community and with local stakeholders and the community, to combat illegal wildlife trade and safeguard our planet's natural heritage.

sections.label: Offence for illegally-traded CITES species
sections.summary: It is an offence to possess or facilitate the sale of illegally-traded CITES species.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: As I explained earlier, it is an offence to possess or facilitate the sale of illegally-traded CITES species.

sections.label: Reviewing rewards for informers
sections.summary: The framework for informer rewards is being reviewed, and the amendment protects informers' identities because tip-offs are relied on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The second point that he raised was around the reward for the informers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I mentioned in my clarification that we are exploring and reviewing this framework and we are not closed to this idea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: So, give us some time, we are looking into this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It is an important area and that is why we have moved in this Act, in this amendment, to protect the identity of such informers because we rely on tip-offs and many of these informants to give us the tip-offs and the information for us to do our operations and enforcement.
